title: Infra GPU Fleet Capacity, CI/CD, and IaC Best Practices
author: Aisha Kapoor
summary: Consolidated team wiki covering GPU fleet sizing, cloud account and VPC networking guardrails, Terraform module patterns, CI/CD pipeline templates, and operational runbooks for capacity and upgrade events.
content:
Overview

This page consolidates operational best practices for Redwood's GPU fleet and related infrastructure: capacity planning, cloud account/networking guardrails, Terraform/IaC module patterns, CI/CD build/deploy pipelines, and runbook procedures. The intention is to provide a single reference for infra engineers and SREs who operate GPU-backed inference capacity across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private offerings.

Scope

- GPU fleet sizing and autoscaling policies (spot vs reserved pools)
- Cloud accounts and VPC design patterns for multi-tenant and customer-isolated deployments
- Terraform module conventions and module registry layout
- CI/CD templates for build -> test -> deploy of infra modules and runtime images
- Runbooks for capacity incidents, rolling upgrades, and emergency scale-outs

Principles and goals

1) Predictability: predictable per-GPU throughput and tail latency; capacity plans tied to SLOs.
2) Safety-first: changes are reviewed, staged in non-prod, and feature-flagged for production rollout.
3) Reusability: standard Terraform modules and CI templates to reduce per-service divergence.
4) Observability: cost + performance telemetry per pool, per-region, and per-customer.

Ownership and contacts

- Infra GPU Fleet: infra-gpu-team (primary), eng-sre (secondary)
- Terraform modules / IaC registry: infra-iac (primary)
- CI/CD pipelines & images: infra-ci (primary)
- On-call: infra-sre rotation; see /confluence/eng-sre/oncall-schedule

Key operational metrics and SLOs

- Cluster-level GPU utilization target: 55% average (allow short bursts to 80%)
- Queue wait time SLO (for Dedicated queued requests): 95th percentile <= 150ms
- Inference tail latency SLO (p95 token latency): <= 200ms for standard models on p4d-like hardware
- On-call alert thresholds: unreserved GPU free capacity < 5% for > 10m; spot eviction rate > 10% in 5m window
- Cost target: unit inference cost per 1k tokens within 10% of benchmark for model class

Capacity planning and formulas

Baseline inputs
- Model throughput per GPU (tokens/s) = measured from benchmarking harness per model and sequence length distribution
- Expected QPS (requests/s) and avg tokens per request (T)

Capacity calculation (simplified)
1) Effective tokens/s required = QPS * T
2) Required GPUs = ceil( Effective tokens/s / (GPU_tokens_per_second * Batch_efficiency_factor) )
3) Add buffer: +20% for unexpected bursts and rollout slack

Example:
- Measured GPU_tokens_per_second = 1200 tokens/s for model A at production batch settings
- QPS = 25, T = 120 tokens => Effective tokens/s = 3000
- Required GPUs = ceil(3000 / (1200 * 0.85)) = ceil(2.94) = 3 GPUs -> provision 4 GPUs (20% buffer)

Pool strategy and labeling

- Reserved pools: customer-dedicated and baseline shared pools (stable latency, paid capacity).
- Spot pools: cost-optimized; used for low-priority workloads with eviction fallback.
- Burst pools: fast-scaling ephemeral capacity (hot spare), regional.

Naming and tags (Terraform + cloud tags)
- Tags: team, env, pool-type, model-class, owner
- Example: {"team":"infra-gpu","env":"prod","pool-type":"reserved","model-class":"decoder-only"}

Cloud accounts and networking guardrails

Account layout
- Per-environment accounts: prod, staging, nonprod, dev, and special accounts for Dedicated/customer-isolated deployments
- Shared services account for observability, artifact registry, and IaC pipeline runners

VPC and subnet patterns
- VPC-per-region with segmented subnets: control-plane (private), inference-workers (private), management (bastion, jump), public egress (nat gateways)
- Use prefix lists and security policies to restrict egress to artifact registries, KMS endpoints, and metrics endpoints

Cross-account connectivity
- Use VPC Peering or AWS Transit Gateway depending on scale; prefer TGW for > 3 accounts per region
- PrivateLink for exposing control plane services to Dedicated/Private customer deployments to avoid public endpoints

Networking guardrails
- No public IPs on inference worker instances by default
- Egress only via managed NAT gateways or centralized egress proxies with TLS inspection if required by compliance
- Flow logs enabled and shipped to central observability account with 90-day retention by default

Terraform / IaC module patterns

Module structure guidelines
- Modules live in the infra-iac monorepo and are published to the internal module registry. Module names should be short and descriptive: "vpc", "gpu-pool", "autoscaler", "iam-roles", "artifact-caching".
- Each module must include: README.md, inputs.tf (document inputs and defaults), outputs.tf, examples/ directory, and an integration test in tests/ using terratest or kitchen-terraform.
- Keep modules small and composable; avoid monolithic modules that manage both networking and compute.

GPU pool module (recommended inputs)
- name (string)
- region (string)
- instance_type (string) e.g. p4d.24xlarge, a100 80GB variants
- desired_capacity (number)
- max_capacity (number)
- min_capacity (number)
- spot_percentage (number)
- scaling_policies (map)

Example Terraform snippet
```
module "gpu_pool_modela_prod" {
  source = "git::ssh://git@internal/repo/infra-iac//modules/gpu-pool?ref=v1.3.0"
  name = "modela-prod-reserved"
  region = "us-west-2"
  instance_type = "p4d.24xlarge"
  desired_capacity = 8
  min_capacity = 6
  max_capacity = 12
  spot_percentage = 0
  scaling_policies = {
    cpu_utilization = { target = 55 }
  }
}
```

Module release process
- Follow semantic versioning. Releases require: (a) passing module unit/integration tests, (b) review by infra-iac, (c) merge to main, and (d) tag and publish to internal registry.

CI/CD pipelines and build templates

Pipeline responsibilities
- Linting/formatting (tflint, tfsec, fmt)
- Unit and integration tests (terratest/test-kitchen)
- Plan and apply gated by PR approval and OPA policy checks
- Blue/green or canary for runtime image deployments (where applicable)

Recommended pipeline layout (example GitHub Actions / internal runner jobs)
1) pre-merge: fmt-check, tflint, static-scan (tfsec), unit-tests
2) merge: terraform plan -> upload artifact
3) gated apply: manual approval OR auto-apply in nonprod; production applies require 2 approvers (infra-iac + owning team)
4) post-apply: integration smoke tests, telemetry sanity checks, rollback window monitoring

Sample GH Actions job for module plan
```
name: Terraform Plan
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  plan:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: Setup Terraform
        uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@v1
      - name: Terraform Init
        run: terraform init -backend-config="bucket=redwood-terraform-state"
      - name: Terraform Plan
        run: terraform plan -out=tfplan
      - name: Upload Plan
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v3
        with:
          name: tfplan
          path: tfplan
```

Runtime image CI/CD
- Build reproducible images using pinned base images and SBOM generation
- Scan images (trivy/clair) and block deploys with high-critical findings
- Use image tags: <commit-sha>-<date> and keep immutable tags for prod releases

Runbooks (procedures)

1) Capacity incident: low free GPUs
- Trigger: alert when unreserved GPU free capacity < 5% for 10m
- Action steps:
  1. Acknowledge alert in PagerDuty and notify #infra-oncall channel
  2. Confirm cause via metrics: check cluster utilization, recent deploys, and scaling events (Grafana dashboards)
  3. If autoscaler active but not scaling: inspect autoscaler logs (kubectl -n infra logs autoscaler-*) and scaling controller metrics in Datadog
  4. If autoscaler healthy: trigger manual scale-up for the affected pool via terraform or cloud console as temporary mitigation: terraform apply -var "desired_capacity=<new>" module/gpu_pool
  5. Post-incident: open a ticket, run RCA, and consider permanent capacity increase or changed scaling policy

2) Rolling upgrade of runtime images on GPU fleet
- Pre-checks: validate canary image on non-prod, run perf benchmarks, and run smoke tests against canary pool
- Rolling strategy: batch-size determined by capacity buffer (recommended: replace 10-20% of pool at a time), wait for healthy checks and p95 latency validation before next batch
- Commands: use our deployment toolchain: infractl deploy --pool <pool> --image <image-tag> --batch-size 10% --health-check "p95_latency < 200ms"
- If health check fails: abort, roll back to previous image, and escalate to runtime team

3) Spot eviction surge
- Detect: spike in eviction metric > 10% per 5m
- Immediate actions: shift traffic to reserved pools via smart routing (console route override) and trigger burst pool spin-up
- Longer term: audit workloads on spot pools and move critical workloads to reserved/burst pools

Change management and safe deploy checklist

- All infra changes require: PR, module tests passing, 2 reviewers (one from infra-iac, one from owning team), and OPA policy pass
- Production Terraform apply requires two distinct approvers unless emergency (emergency requires post-facto audit and two approvers within 24h)

Observability and dashboards

Essential dashboards:
- GPU Fleet Overview: per-pool GPU count, allocation, avg PCR (packets/compute ratio), utilization histogram, spot eviction rate
- Per-region cost and unit-cost trends
- Autoscaler health and scaling event timeline
- Model-level latency and error rates aggregated by pool

Logging and retention
- Infrastructure logs: 90 days
- Audit logs (IAM, terraform state changes): 1 year by default for compliance accounts

Common pitfalls and mitigation

- Over-provisioning due to inaccurate benchmark inputs: ensure periodic re-benchmarking every quarter and after major model changes
- Drift between module versions: pin module versions in service stacks and run scheduled dependency updates via Dependabot-style automation
- Inconsistent tagging: enforce tags via Terragrunt or policy-as-code gate in CI

Appendices

A. Common commands
- View autoscaler logs: kubectl -n infra logs deploy/autoscaler --since=1h
- Manual scale (terraform): terraform apply -target=module.gpu_pool -var 'desired_capacity=8'
- Check spot eviction events (Cloud provider CLI): aws ec2 describe-spot-instance-requests --filters ...

B. Example terraform module checklist (PR template)
- [ ] README updated with inputs/outputs
- [ ] examples/ tested
- [ ] terratest or integration test added/updated
- [ ] tflint/tfsec clean
- [ ] OPA policy checks pass

C. Links and references
- GPU benchmarking harness: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/benchmarking-harness
- Module registry: internal://terraform-registry/infra-iac
- Infra runbooks: /confluence/eng-infra/runbooks
